front_hand PhD ombuds
The success of a PhD depends on the mutual commitment of the doctoral researcher and the supervisor and on the harmonious relationship between them.
If you have any doubts or concerns or if you encounter a disagreement with your supervisor, we encourage you to contact the ombudsteam.
All ombuds persons have received a training and are in the best position to find a solution. They will treat your concerns in all objectivity and in strict confidentiality.
More information

start Getting started
The charter of the PhD researcher and the supervisor
The charter of the PhD researcher and the supervisor is an appendix to the University Doctoral Regulations and discusses the mutual expectations and responsibilities of both PhD researcher and supervisor.
At the start of the PhD, both the PhD researcher and the supervisor need to confirm that they have read and discussed the charter and have made the necessary arrangements to ensure a smooth PhD.
Consult the charter
Enrolment
When you begin your doctoral studies, you must enrol in a doctoral programme.
Important Please note that you must re-enrol every academic year.

Legal status
The academic staff comprises three main staff groups: the AAP, BAP and ZAP. Each staff group in turn comprises a number of staff categories, each with its own finality.
The staff categories are based on (decree) regulations and aim to make the framework of employment conditions, career development and agreements as compatible as possible with the finality of the staff category.
You can learn more about different staff categories here.

route Integrated learning path 'Responsible and Open Research' for PhD researchers
Aim
To support PhD researchers in their development.
Learn more
Goals
to conduct your research in a reliable, honest and transparent manner;
to communicate about your research in an open and responsible way, and to share your knowledge and results with the (research) community.
Do I have to?
Apart from some compulsory components, PhD researchers can accomplish the recommended components in a flexible way that suits their needs.

share Generative Artificial Intelligence guidelines
Guidelines for Responsible use of GenAI in research
KU Leuven encourages researchers to use GenAI technology in a responsible and critical manner. Through these guidelines, we want to make researchers aware of the usability of the technology in research, its limitations and risks. We aim to support them in using these new tools with integrity and ethics in mind, similar as with all other tools, in all phases of scientific research from conceptualization to dissemination of results.
